title: Website analytics — remove the visitor opt-out

steps.headline: Remove the visitor opt-out and keep a plain privacy disclosure?
steps.today: The earlier approved checklist requires a visitor opt-out. You rejected its preview and asked to remove it because the measurements are basic.
steps.problem: The checklist and implementation must reflect your revised choice. Limited analytics still involves page-level records and hosting-provider processing; it is not risk-free.
steps.proposal: Remove the analytics toggle, its dialog, and browser preference storage. Keep the existing Privacy link and an accurate disclosure of visits, setup-instruction opens, download clicks, campaign attribution, temporary page grouping and 90-day history. No analytics cookies, fingerprinting, returning-visitor identity or links to app-device records. Collection remains off until cost, security and applicable privacy requirements are checked; this decision does not certify legal compliance or authorize activation.

options.label: Remove the opt-out
pros: Removes the visitor toggle and its stored preference.
cons: Visitors cannot disable measurement through the website itself.
Disclosure and applicable privacy requirements still need checking before activation.

options.label: Keep an opt-out
pros: Visitors retain an explicit website control.
cons: Keeps a control you said is unnecessary; its design would need another pass.
